My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger

issues.item: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: For a man-made disaster trauma in a 58-year-old forensic analyst, this item is only coherent if there was a significant physical injury. The rest of the selected profile does not support an injury-based presentation: the threat items emphasize environmental danger and vigilance (limited safe places, loud sounds, unfamiliar places), while the other appraisals are about coping failure and loss of capability rather than concrete bodily injury. With no memory or strategy items to anchor a physical-injury narrative, this appraisal stands out as clinically hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Threat: Safe Zone Only: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places
issues.explanation: The profile is not coherent with the supplied cognitive formulation because all cross-node edges are inactive, which implies these components should not appear as tightly linked aspects of one maintaining pattern. However, the Threat items and Negative Appraisal items are strongly conceptually connected: perceiving the world as dangerous maps directly onto restricted safety zones and avoidance of unfamiliar places, creating an active Threat–Negative Appraisal linkage that contradicts the formulation.

issues.item: Threat: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
issues.explanation: Within the selected nodes, the content clusters into a classic mutually reinforcing danger/coping pattern rather than isolated components. 'World is a dangerous place' coheres directly with hypervigilance to sounds and avoidance of unfamiliar places, while 'Bad Coper' and 'No longer capable' reflect generalized post-trauma self-evaluation likely tied to the same threat response. With no active edges anywhere in the formulation, this degree of integration is inconsistent.

issues.item: Threat in Sounds: I am on high alert when I hear unexpected or loud sounds
issues.explanation: The formulation specifies no active edges, so the selected nodes should function as relatively isolated components rather than implying a tight linked syndrome. Here the Threat items and Negative Appraisal items form a classic connected PTSD pattern: danger-focused hypervigilance/startle and avoidance are closely mirrored by broad beliefs that the world is dangerous and that the self is incapable. This actively implies strong Threat↔Negative Appraisal linkage, which contradicts the fully disconnected formulation.

issues.item: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
issues.explanation: Within Threat, the items are coherent with each other, and within Negative Appraisals the items are also coherent. The problem is cross-node/formulation consistency: the profile presents mutually reinforcing danger sensitivity and negative self/world beliefs despite all edges being inactive.

vignette: Carlos Hernandez still remembers the acrid smell of smoke and ash that lingered in his clothes for days after the warehouse fire. As a forensic analyst, he had processed countless crime scenes, but nothing could have prepared him for the devastation he witnessed that day. The screams of trapped workers, the desperate attempts to escape, and the eerie silence that followed still echo in his mind. In the months following the disaster, Carlos began to notice changes in himself. He felt jumpy, always on edge, as if waiting for the next explosion or collapse. Simple noises – a car backfiring, a door slamming shut – made him flinch. His body had become a coiled spring, constantly tense and ready to react to danger. His colleagues at the lab would often comment on his heightened startle response, but Carlos just shrugged it off as a side effect of the long hours he'd been putting in. As time passed, Carlos found himself increasingly hesitant to venture into unfamiliar places. He avoided traveling for work, citing concerns about safety and security. Even routine errands became daunting tasks; he would find excuses to send his wife, Elena, instead. His reasoning was simple: if he couldn't assess the danger himself, how could he trust anyone else to keep him safe? This new habit had started as a minor inconvenience but soon snowballed into a full-blown avoidance strategy. Carlos's self-doubt also began to creep in, casting a shadow over his professional identity. He'd always prided himself on being a meticulous and level-headed forensic analyst, but the warehouse fire seemed to have shaken him to his core. Now, he questioned whether he was truly capable of handling high-pressure situations. His reactions since the event – the jumpiness, the avoidance behaviors – convinced him that he was no longer the competent professional he once was. The world itself had also become a more menacing place in Carlos's eyes. He couldn't shake the feeling that danger lurked around every corner, waiting to pounce. The fire had been a stark reminder of how quickly life could spiral out of control. His friends and family would try to reassure him, but he just couldn't seem to shake off the sense of unease. Elena noticed the changes in Carlos too – the way he'd freeze up at sudden noises, the way he'd hesitate before leaving the house. She tried to be supportive, but it was clear that Carlos's struggles were affecting their relationship. He became withdrawn and isolated, pushing away even those closest to him. One day, while working late in the lab, Carlos found himself staring blankly at a stack of files, his mind a thousand miles away. The realization hit him like a ton of bricks: he couldn't keep living like this. The avoidance behaviors, the constant hypervigilance – it was all taking a toll on his mental and physical health. With Elena's encouragement, Carlos finally made the decision to seek help, hoping that someone could guide him back to the man he once was. As he sat in the therapist's office, fidgeting with his hands, Carlos couldn't help but wonder if he'd ever be able to shake off the ghosts of the warehouse fire. Would he be able to reclaim his sense of self, or would the memories continue to haunt him? The uncertainty hung heavy in the air, a constant reminder that the journey ahead would not be easy.
